notes.english: Working language. Collide public-domain English Bibles verse by verse. Apparent error in English is a pointer, not the verdict.
notes.greek_hebrew: Control languages. Used to classify an English collision as inner-English style, source-text fork (TR/CT, MT/LXX/DSS), or canon.
notes.chaldean: In older English (KJV headings, lexicons) 'Chaldee' usually means Biblical Aramaic (Daniel, Ezra) and sometimes Targum. It is not a third Semitic original beside Hebrew and Aramaic. Parked until the Aramaic desk is open.

sources.label: Wycliffe
sources.role: Late medieval English; Vulgate-shaped. Residue often Latin, not Greek.

sources.label: Tyndale (NT / Pentateuch)
sources.role: First printed English from Greek/Hebrew. Ancestor of Geneva and KJV diction.

sources.label: Coverdale 1535
sources.role: First complete printed English Bible; mixes Tyndale, Latin, German.

sources.label: Geneva 1560 / 1599
sources.role: The Reformation English Bible. Notes are residue of how readers inhabited the text.

sources.label: KJV 1769 (Blayney)
sources.role: The default English 'how it has been' for Protestant print. OT from MT, NT from Textus Receptus. 1611 Apocrypha is canon residue.

sources.label: Douay-Rheims (Challoner)
sources.role: English of the Vulgate. Collides with KJV wherever Latin and Hebrew/Greek part ways.

sources.label: Webster 1833
sources.role: KJV diction with American regularization. Useful as a near-KJV control.

sources.label: Young's Literal Translation
sources.role: English that tries to keep Hebrew/Greek tense and word order. Good for spotting smoothing in other English.

sources.label: American Standard Version 1901
sources.role: Early critical-text English. The hinge between KJV-type and modern Protestant Bibles.

sources.label: JPS Tanakh 1917
sources.role: Jewish English of the Masoretic OT. No NT; no Christian recension at the English layer.

sources.label: Brenton English Septuagint
sources.role: English of the Greek OT. The other Old Testament in English. Primary residue hunter vs KJV/JPS.

sources.label: World English Bible
sources.role: Modern public-domain-ish English. Use for 'how it is now' without copyright walls.

sources.label: Swete Septuagint
sources.role: Greek OT control. Prefer diplomatic PD editions over copyrighted Rahlfs-Hanhart for the corpus itself.

sources.label: Westcott-Hort 1881
sources.role: The Greek NT that pulled English off the Textus Receptus. Pair with KJV to see NT residue.

sources.label: Westminster Leningrad Codex (consonantal)
sources.role: Diplomatic Masoretic control. Morphology layers may be licensed; consonants are the usual public working text.
